# Tokamak The tokamak is a fusion engine. A magnetic field holds a cloud of plasma inside the [bold]core[/bold], [bold]gyrotrons[/bold] heat the plasma, and [bold]fuel injectors[/bold] feed it fuel rods. The hotter the plasma, the more power the core puts onto the [textlink="high voltage network" link="VoltageNetworks"], up to 5 MW.
It is a demanding engine. There is no coolant loop: the plasma only loses heat slowly by itself, and it gets harder to hold the hotter and busier it is. Left alone it ruptures, which wrecks the room and irradiates the area.
## The parts - [bold]Core.[/bold] Holds up to 400 units of plasma. Connects to the grid with an HV cable and also needs ordinary APC power to keep its field up. - [bold]Gyrotron.[/bold] Fires microwave pulses along a straight line to heat the plasma. - [bold]Fuel injector.[/bold] Holds one fuel rod and feeds it into the plasma along a straight line. - [bold]Harvester.[/bold] Optional. Pulls silver and gold out of the plasma and presses them into sheets. - [bold]Console.[/bold] Starts and stops the field, sets its strength, and controls every device around the core. It also has the SCRAM button.
## Getting one The tokamak is unlocked by the [bold]Fusion Power[/bold] technology in the Industrial discipline, which needs Nuclear Power Generation first. It unlocks the console board and all of the fuel rod designs.
Cargo also sells the parts as flatpacks and crates: the core, a pair of gyrotrons, a pair of injectors, a harvester, a console board and a starter crate of four deuterium-tritium rods. Unpack flatpacks to build the machines.
